description: Backend LEGO registry: the single machine-readable source of truth for backend domain boundaries, ownership, public contracts, declared dependencies and capabilities. Supports hierarchical LEGO (parent -> sub-LEGO -> sub-sub-LEGO) via the `parent` field: a nested entry is a domain like any other, so ownership, contracts, versioning and the dependency gate work identically at every level. Validated by apps/n8n-lego/src/lego/registry.mjs and enforced by tools/lego/architecture-gate.mjs.

domains.title: Platform kernel (shared primitives)
domains.notes: Shared kernel. Only cross-domain primitives may live here: process configuration and structured logging. It is a graph leaf — it must never import a domain.

domains.title: Backend LEGO foundation (registry, error contract, versioning)

operations.name: stream
operations.backpressureReason: The generic stream primitive blocks by default: a producer faster than its consumer should be slowed, not buffered. A caller that wants a lossy policy chooses one explicitly.

domains.notes: The socket system itself: domain registry, machine-readable error codes and the contract lock. Pure data + pure functions; may not depend on any domain.

domains.title: AI Foundation contracts and Context & Session foundation

operations.name: stream
operations.backpressureReason: Token streams block. Dropping tokens would corrupt the output, and buffering an unbounded generation is how a low-end device runs out of memory.

operations.name: stream
operations.backpressureReason: Agent progress updates coalesce: only the latest state matters, and a slow consumer should see current progress rather than a replay of every intermediate step.

capabilities.notes: P2.13 implementation target: bounded session identity/state, explicit lifecycle transitions, parent references and context/continuation linkage. A session never contains an unbounded transcript.

operations.name: subscribe
operations.backpressureReason: Event subscribers get drop-oldest: recent events are more useful than stale ones, and an event stream must never stall the agent producing it.

capabilities.notes: P2.13 implementation target: bounded context registry, selective load, compaction ancestry, deterministic rollover, continuation serialization, rehydration and explicit continuity verification. No model/runtime/provider dependency.

Skill REGISTRY, implemented in P2.12: registration, validation, lazy discovery and lifecycle. Skills are declarative documents; nothing executes a procedure. A skill declares requiredCapabilities and never grants them — the capability system stays the authority. Declared here rather than as a new top-level domain because XA-11 (is a skill a backend concept at all?) is open-for-manager.

P2.14 bounded memory: persistent knowledge that survives context replacement, scope-isolated, checksum-verified, provider-replaceable. Four operations only: remember/recall/list/forget. No vector search, no auto-embed, no model dependency. Provider is the persistence boundary.

P2.16 bounded execution foundation (ai.agent-machine@1.1.0): machine/agent/task identity, canonical agent lifecycle incl. ready, bounded step bookkeeping, first-class budgets, registry-validated capability scope, bounded delegation bookkeeping (narrowed grants, clamped budget/deadline, no inheritance), bounded graph validation, deterministic event derivation and a replaceable provider/executor seam. Consumes ai.context, ai.agent-session, ai.memory and ai.workspace by opaque reference only. Nine operations, five ai:agent:* permissions; no close, no loop, no inference, no tools, no shell, no filesystem, no process, no child execution. The contract-only ai.agent-runtime capability above it remains the declared shape of the future full loop, which builds on this foundation.

P2.24 implementation target: honest accounting records (reported/estimated/unavailable, never fabricated zero), scope-filtered queries, budget views over what was actually recorded. Cost derivation is a pure exported function, not an operation. No provider integration, no telemetry capture, no billing.

domains.notes: Contract-only. Declares vocabulary for a future AI Foundation: provider/runtime taxonomy, model and tool gateways, application providers, agent lifecycle, session, delegation, events, decision, approval, artifact and context. NOTHING is implemented: no inference, no agent loop, no gateway client, no MCP server or client, no network call, no new dependency. Owned by manager because these contracts are cross-domain and must not be owned by whoever writes the first adapter. A dependency-free leaf: the AI Foundation must never become a prerequisite for the backend booting. P2.12: the Skill registry (src/lego/skill.mjs) reads the capability registry from lego-foundation to answer whether a skill's required capabilities are DECLARED. The direction is deliberate and one-way: the AI Foundation consumes the capability registry, the capability registry knows nothing about AI. This is the dependency that keeps Skill from copying the capability list, which would be the real architectural failure — two registries disagreeing about what exists. lego-foundation does not depend on ai-foundation, so no cycle is created, and the AI Foundation is still not required for the backend to boot.
domains.statusNote: P2.16 implements the Agent Machine execution FOUNDATION (src/lego/agent-machine.mjs, ai.agent-machine@1.0.0): bounded identity, lifecycle, step bookkeeping, budgets, deterministic transitions and a provider/executor seam, consuming Context, Session, Memory and Workspace by opaque reference only. Skill is complete from P2.12; Context & Session from P2.13; Memory from P2.14; Workspace from P2.15. The AI runtime (model inference, agent loop, delegation, parallelism, MCP) remains unimplemented: agent-machine keeps status contract-only in the AI set.

domains.title: Compatibility layer (frontend <-> backend boundary)
domains.notes: Translates route semantics, auth context, envelopes, errors and capability state. Business logic is forbidden here — it translates, it does not decide.

domains.title: Auth (session, accounts, permission model)
domains.notes: P5.1 note: 'public' stays [] deliberately. Publishing src/auth/security here would switch on R4 boundary policing for this domain and immediately expose a PRE-EXISTING internal reach that P5 does not own: src/auth/contract/index.mjs (domain auth.identity, owner agent-3) re-exports toPublicUser/hasOwner from src/auth.mjs. That coupling predates P5 and is out of P5.1 scope; retiring it is an agent-3/P5.x follow-up. Until then the contract-lock row is the publication mechanism for auth.principal, which is how node-registry (33 rows), execution (5) and workflow (2) already operate.

domains.title: Auth identity projection (read-only)
domains.notes: Deliberately a dependency-free LEAF exposing exactly two pure read-only functions: toPublicUser (projection) and hasOwner (boolean). It holds no authority: nothing here can create a session, verify a password or mint a token. Being a leaf is what lets the compatibility layer depend on it without a cycle back into auth's HTTP adapter. Surface pinned by test/lego-boundary.test.mjs.

domains.title: Dynamic node parameters
domains.notes: P7-S01 ships the ParameterPlan compiler (src/lego/parameter-plan.mjs, pure, no I/O). P7-S02 adds the RESOLVE stage (src/lego/parameter-graph.mjs, pure, no I/O): the n8n displayParameter visibility port, the parameter dependency graph and the incremental ResolutionSession. domains.title: Webhook / trigger ingress

capabilities.note: P4-S01 / Issue #111 item 2. Predictive admission controller (full). Observes latency, queue depth, CPU/memory pressure, admission rate, completion rate, error rate and recent burst shape; adjusts ONLY per-route concurrency, per-workflow concurrency, queue budget, low-priority admission and defer threshold. Hard ceilings are immutable; stale telemetry forces a conservative fallback, never aggressive admission. AdmissionTargets carries no security/permission/authentication field, so adaptation structurally cannot widen authority or bypass authentication, and queue budget is always bounded by the observed queue capacity.

P4-S01 / Issue #111 item 9. Shadow compatibility path. Compares reference (canonical) vs candidate (optimized) P4 behaviour on route selection, status, response shape, admission, error and observable ordering. Reference and candidate are pure functions; candidate side effects are always suppressed so a real external side effect is never duplicated. Default Disabled = canonical n8n behaviour.

P4-S01 / Issue #111 item 10. P4 self-profiling: optional, low-overhead, off by default. Records route lookup time, admission time, queue wait, payload-copy cost, allocation pressure and slow route patterns. Collection is hard-bounded (max_samples) and derived state can be reset. eBPF is complementary on Linux only and never becomes a P4 runtime dependency.

P4-S01 / Issue #225 item 1. Dedicated webhook/ingress plane: separates webhook intake from editor/API and execution workers, with bounded request buffering, admission control and response streaming/offload. Each plane owns a separate budget so a webhook burst cannot consume control-plane capacity and the UI/API stay responsive. Full buffer rejects rather than queueing without bound.

domains.notes: Ownership is provisional; Manager must confirm webhook stays with Agent 2 (workflow/execution) rather than Agent 6 (runtime).

allowances.reason: Execution ids come from the storage counter; the storage domain has no contract module yet.
allowances.resolution: Publish src/storage/contract/index.mjs (id allocation + collection ports) and consume that.
allowances.reviewNote: P2.9: NARROWED, not removed. The import is exactly one symbol (newExecutionId) in exactly one file (src/engine.mjs). It cannot be retired the way A1/A2 were, because unlike toPublicUser/hasOwner this is not a pure read-only projection — it mutates a process-local counter, and that counter IS scale-out blocker S2. Publishing a storage contract that merely re-exports newExecutionId would retire the allowance while preserving the blocker, i.e. it would make the gate greener and the architecture no safer. Retiring A3 correctly requires agent-5 to design durable id allocation (P8). Guarded by test/lego-boundary.test.mjs: the allowance may not grow beyond this one symbol in this one file.

allowances.reason: P5.4 must release credential secrets through the existing P2.27 Secret Broker (issue #217 hard rule: 'do not create another broker'). The broker IS a locked published contract - lego.plugin-runtime@0.10.0, owner agent-1 - which declares exactly ['PLUGIN_SECRET_LIMITS','createSecretBroker'] as its exports. It is absent from lego-foundation's domain `public:` list, which is owned by manager, so it cannot be published from this slice. Without the allowance P5.4 would have to build a second broker, which is the one outcome the issue forbids.
allowances.resolution: Ask manager to add 'src/lego/plugin-secrets.mjs' to the lego-foundation domain `public:` list. No new code is required: the file is already a locked contract surface (lego.plugin-runtime@0.10.0) and already publishes only these two symbols. Once that one line lands, delete A4.
allowances.reviewNote: P5.4: NARROWED to the minimum that satisfies 'do not create another broker'. The import is exactly two symbols (createSecretBroker, PLUGIN_SECRET_LIMITS) in exactly one file, and secret-ref.mjs is the ONLY importer - every other consumer of the broker, including all of P5.4, goes through the SecretRef authority. The alternative (a parallel broker) is explicitly forbidden by #217, and re-implementing the broker's single-use/TTL/live-cap semantics locally would be both more code and less safe. Guarded by test/lego-credentials.test.mjs: the allowance may not grow beyond these two symbols in this one file.

rules: No new file may be added to the legacy zone: the file list above is frozen and checked by the architecture gate.
No new business logic in the zone; only carve-outs leave it.
The zone may import domain internals (temporarily); new domains may not.
Nothing may import the legacy zone except the composition root.
The aggregate may only shrink. test/lego-boundary.test.mjs pins its line count at its P2.7 high-water mark of 845.

New LEGO functionality must NOT be added here. A new capability gets its own domain with its own contract, and the compatibility layer routes to it — that is the strangler path, and it is the only one.
A route family with no legitimate owner is recorded in legacy.unresolvedOwnership and escalated, never assigned to a convenient domain to make the map look finished.

unresolvedOwnership.currentBehaviour: constant empty object; no business logic
unresolvedOwnership.why: These are i18n surfaces. The project has an explicit standing decision NOT to build a Translation LEGO or language packs, so there is no domain that legitimately owns them. Assigning them to node-registry or credentials would manufacture ownership to make a map look complete, and would put i18n responsibility inside domains that have no i18n mandate.
unresolvedOwnership.question: Who owns editor-facing i18n surfaces while Translation remains out of scope — compatibility as a permanent stub custodian, or a future Translation LEGO?

unresolvedOwnership.why: Environment variables are an enterprise feature spanning workspace scoping, storage and RBAC. No current domain has a mandate, and the three plausible owners (workspace, storage, settings) each own only part.
unresolvedOwnership.question: Does 'variables' become a workspace-scoped storage feature (agent-5 + agent-2) or stay a compatibility stub until an enterprise phase?

stubFamilies.note: These families return constants and contain NO business logic. They are compatibility stubs that keep the editor booting, not features living in the wrong place. Carving them out would move a one-line constant into a new file and call it architecture; they are listed so the distinction stays visible and so nobody mistakes the line count for un-migrated domain logic.
stubFamilies.rule: A stub family may only leave the legacy zone when the owning domain implements it for real. Until then it stays here and MUST NOT grow beyond returning a constant.

strangler.path: legacy REST -> compatibility boundary -> backend LEGO contracts
carveOutProcedure: 1. Pick one route family from migrationTargets.
2. The TARGET domain (not agent-1) implements it behind its own contract.
3. Register the contract surface in contract-lock.json.
4. src/server.mjs mounts the new domain's routes BEFORE the legacy router.
5. Delete the handlers from src/rest/routes.mjs — the line count must drop.
6. Re-run npm run lego:gate; the boundary test proves the aggregate shrank.
strangler.antiPattern: Do not create a second aggregate. Three route families in one new 'misc' LEGO is the same mistake with a newer filename.

rules: A sub-LEGO is a full registry entry with `parent` set to its parent's id. It declares its own owner, contract version, dependencies, capabilities and tests.
Nest only where the split is justified by a real boundary. Depth is capped at 3 (parent -> child -> grandchild) to prevent decorative hierarchies.
A sub-LEGO's paths must live inside its parent's paths — a child cannot own code outside its parent.
A sub-LEGO inherits nothing implicitly: dependencies and forbidden directions are declared per entry.
A parent may reach its own children's public contracts without declaring a dependency (composition inside one domain); reaching a child's internals is still forbidden.
An outside consumer may depend on a sub-LEGO's public contract only if it declares that sub-LEGO in dependsOn. Sibling-internal reach (A.sub -> B.sub internal) is always forbidden.
A sub-LEGO may be owned by a different agent than its parent; ownership remains single-writer at every level.

scaleOut.principle: A LEGO contract must not assume it is the only process. P2.7 implements no worker, queue or scaling infrastructure — it only checks, and records, whether the logical contracts could survive being moved into a second process. Checked by tools/lego/scale-out-readiness.mjs.
rules: New LEGO code (contract-first domains, the foundation, templates) must be process-agnostic: no module-global mutable state, no process-local id allocation, no direct filesystem or env access. Findings there fail the build outright.
Existing code may have findings, but every one must be declared here with a domain, an owner, a severity and a resolution plan. Undeclared findings fail.
An exception that no longer matches anything is stale and fails — the list shrinks, it does not rot.
A construct that matches a pattern but is genuinely process-safe may be justified in place with `// @scale-out-safe: <reason>`; the reason is reviewed like code.

No LEGO may reach another LEGO's database/persistence internals, in one process or many. That is already enforced by the dependency gate (R2/R4), which is what makes a future process split a deployment change rather than a redesign.
blockingForScaleOut: src/store.mjs S3 (local JSON files as the system of record)

exceptions.reason: newExecutionId() hands out ids from a module-scope counter seeded at boot. Two processes would issue the same execution ids.
exceptions.resolution: Move id allocation behind the storage contract (a durable sequence). This is the single hardest blocker to multi-process execution.

exceptions.reason: The system of record is JSON files on local disk, written with writeFileSync + renameSync. A second worker on another host sees none of it.
exceptions.resolution: Keep the collection contract, replace the backend with a shared store. The contract shape already allows it; only the implementation is local.

exceptions.reason: Module-scope counter state (same construct as S2).
exceptions.resolution: Removed together with S2 when id allocation moves behind the contract.

exceptions.reason: Module-scope memoization of the immutable node catalog read from disk at boot.
exceptions.resolution: Harmless per process (every worker would load the identical pinned catalog), but should become an injected, explicitly-scoped cache when the node registry is carved out.

exceptions.reason: Module-scope roles cache (roles.json is static and ships with the package); resetRolesCache() already exists for tests.
exceptions.resolution: Same as the catalog: identical in every process. Fold into an injected registry when the auth contract is published.

exceptions.reason: The kernel reads process.env — that is its job: it is the adapter that turns the environment into an injected config object.
exceptions.resolution: Accepted permanently. Config is read once at the edge and injected everywhere else, which is exactly the property that keeps domains process-agnostic.

exceptions.reason: Writes the instance identity file (.instance.json) once at first boot.
exceptions.resolution: Accepted for single-node. A multi-node deployment must provision the instance secret externally instead; documented rather than solved here.

exceptions.reason: The composition root reads process.env to build the config it injects.
exceptions.resolution: Accepted: this is the correct place for it. Nothing downstream of the composition root reads the environment.

exceptions.reason: The CLI reads the environment to construct the runtime.
exceptions.resolution: Accepted: same reason as the composition root.

exceptions.reason: The engine resolves its implementation path from N8N_LEGO_ENGINE_PATH directly instead of receiving it in config.
exceptions.resolution: Move the path into the injected config when the execution contract is published, so the engine has no environment dependency of its own.

exceptions.reason: Reads N8N_LEGO_FRONTEND_PATH directly to resolve where the frontend LEGO package lives, instead of receiving the path in the injected config. Found by the scale-out gate during the P2.11 reconciliation, when agent-1's frontend host was merged in.
exceptions.resolution: Move the override into config.mjs and pass it through, the same way the engine path will be. Not blocking for scale-out: it is a boot-time package-resolution hint, identical on every instance, and it does not carry per-process state.

exceptions.reason: P5.5's initial KeyProvider is local/VPS-native by design (#218): the keyring is one 0600 file in the data directory, written atomically (tmp + fsync + rename). A second worker on another host cannot see it, so it cannot open credentials sealed by this host. This is the same single-host limit as src/store.mjs S3, where the sealed credentials themselves live. Severity is should-fix, not blocking, because it is currently shadowed by that storage blocker: while the sealed records themselves live on one host's disk, a shared keyring would not let a second host read them anyway. It becomes blocking the moment src/store.mjs S3 is resolved (P8) - at that point a shared KeyProvider must land with it.
exceptions.resolution: Keep the KeyProvider contract (currentKeyRef / readableKeyRefs / deriveKey / beginRotation / abortRotation / retire / state) and add a shared provider behind it (an external KMS is explicitly non-scope for P5.5). Callers already depend only on the contract, never on the file, so no caller changes. Scale-out of workers is P11.

exceptions.reason: P5.8 (#221): `n8n-lego credentials backup <file>` writes the encrypted credential backup to a file the OPERATOR names (0600, tmp + rename, never over an existing file). It is an offline CLI export, not runtime state: the server never reads it, and no second worker needs to see it. The command refuses to run mutating verbs while the server is up.
exceptions.resolution: Accepted: an operator export is local by definition. The runtime state it snapshots (credentials + keyring) is already declared under src/store.mjs S3 and src/auth/security/key-provider.mjs S3.

scaleOut.verdict: NOT scale-out ready. Two class-A blockers remain in src/store.mjs. P2.9 did not change this.

legend.A: must be fixed before multi-process / multi-instance execution
legend.B: safe local implementation; correct as-is for a single process

findings.finding: execution ids come from a process-local in-memory counter
findings.consequence: two processes allocate the same execution id; history silently corrupts
findings.boundary: Retiring this is the SAME work as retiring allowance A3. The seam is a storage contract that owns durable id allocation; src/engine.mjs then consumes the contract instead of the module.
findings.notSolvedHere: Designing durable id allocation is agent-5's storage implementation, explicitly out of scope for P2.9.

findings.finding: local JSON on disk is the system of record
findings.consequence: a second instance cannot see the first instance's data
findings.boundary: The storage contract must abstract the collection ports so local JSON -> SQLite -> Postgres is an implementation swap, not a consumer rewrite.
findings.notSolvedHere: Storage engine selection and migration is P8.

findings.finding: module-level cache of the node catalog
findings.consequence: none: the catalog is immutable, derived and identical in every process
none: roles are read-only reference data loaded from a shipped file

findings.finding: the provider registry is process-local by design
findings.consequence: none today; a worker or remote adapter registers the same provider shape with transport!=in-process
findings.note: This is the intended seam for cross-process communication: the contract does not change, only the binding.

findings.consequence: none today; serializeEnvelope already drops the signal and flags cancellable:false at a boundary
findings.note: A worker binding must supply its own cancellation channel. The envelope already says so explicitly rather than pretending the signal survived.

findings.consequence: configuration should arrive through the kernel config contract

findings.finding: environment and path reads at the composition root
findings.consequence: none: the edge is exactly where configuration SHOULD be read

foundation.note: Foundation 1.0 fields (tier, dataOwner, stateOwner, trust, resources, communication, failureBoundary) are declared per domain below and validated by validateRegistry + tools/lego/foundation-gate.mjs.

retiredAllowances.was: compatibility + settings imported src/auth.mjs internals (toPublicUser, hasOwner)
retiredAllowances.resolution: agent-3's auth domain published the dependency-free nested leaf 'auth.identity' (src/auth/contract/index.mjs) exposing exactly toPublicUser + hasOwner; compatibility and settings now depend on that leaf. Modelling it as a leaf rather than widening 'auth' is what avoids a compatibility <-> auth cycle.
retiredAllowances.guard: test/lego-boundary.test.mjs asserts the auth contract surface is exactly [toPublicUser, hasOwner] and that no file outside src/auth/ imports src/auth.mjs.

surfaceAliases.rule: A surface alias maps an external/UI vocabulary word to ONE canonical capability-owning domain. It creates no capability, no contract and no ownership. If two words mean genuinely different things they must be different capabilities, not aliases.
surfaceAliases.why: The editor says "executions" (a collection of records); the architecture says "execution" (the capability of running a workflow). Creating a second capability to match UI plurality would duplicate ownership for a grammatical difference. Aliasing keeps one owner and one contract while the mapping stays deterministic.

aliases.note: Plural UI collection of execution records; the singular capability owns running and inspecting them.
Plural collection; singular capability owns the workflow entity.
Already plural in both vocabularies; recorded so the map is total rather than selective.
The UI word is "project"; the architecture calls the domain workspace. This is a genuine rename, not a plural, which is exactly why it must be declared rather than guessed.
UI speaks of node types; the domain owns the registry that resolves them.

constraints: Every alias must resolve to an existing domain id.
No alias may collide with a real domain id (that would make resolution ambiguous).
No two aliases may share a surface word.
An alias is a read-model convenience for consumers; the backend never resolves ownership through it.
